text:
nina: quick brain-dump from the prefix-caching sync — we've got three recurring failure modes when we promote short leases into durable credit moves: flip-flop promotes, donor crash mid-transfer, and subtle RAWR on long-lived cursors. proposing a 'promotion fence' approach with a watermark probe to catch RAWR risk before finalizing a move.

omar: fence? curious for details. how would watermark probe work at slab scale without too much overhead?

nina: idea sketch: when a lease is candidate for promotion we do a two-step: 1) soft-fence: create a tentative transfer (not applied) and run a shadow-read probe for the prefix for a small sample window to detect any in-flight write cursors or recent tail writes; 2) if probe passes and WAL/escrow path is healthy, flip the fence and commit. If probe shows risk, abort and keep lease as short-lived.

felix: sounds promising. how do we implement shadow-read probe cheaply? we can't read full tenant dataset.

susan: we can probe by sampling active RPC metadata: check last-write-ts for prefix (from txn-metadata cache) and active-cursor-count sampler. also run a small synchronous read against the on-disk store for 1-2 keys at prefix hash sample. cheap and probabilistic but helps catch obvious RAWR exposures.

omar: what about donors crashing between soft-fence and commit? need idempotent moves + recovery.

nina: yes — escrow WAL still used. soft-fence writes a tentative WAL entry like "PROMOTE_PENDING(move_id, lease_id, probe_snapshot_id)". commit path requires WAL append of COMMIT. recovery scans WAL: if PROMOTE_PENDING found without COMMIT after timeout, the reconciler either completes commit (if probe_snapshot still valid) or aborts and refunds lease. move_id is globally unique per-slab to ensure idempotency.

felix: we should define strict invariants. proposal: "AVAILABLE + ESCROW_PENDING + COMMITTED == TOTAL_CREDITS" and "PROMOTE_ONLY_IF(probe_ok && !cursor_hold)". auditors should be able to prove invariants by WAL scan + probe logs.

susan: plus add a compact audit checksum per-tenant that sums credits across slabs every minute and emits an alert if mismatch > epsilon. cheap sanity check to catch rare double-spend or lost-credit bugs.

omar: telemetry needed: promote_attempts, promote_probe_failures, promote_retries, promote_aborts_on_pins, escrow_recovery_actions, stuck_promotes. ops wants percentiles for probe latency too.

nina: rollout plan: feature-flagged. stage 1: read-only probes + counters (no commits). stage 2: enable soft-fence + simulated commits (WAL entries but no actual balance changes). stage 3: enable commit on 1% slabs. stage 4: ramp with automatic rollback if stuck_promotes > threshold. ops kill-switch to freeze new promos cluster-wide.

felix: implementation detail: probe snapshot must be cheap and monotonic. use per-prefix watermark = max(last_write_ts, last_cursor_update_ts). snapshot_id = (watermark_ts, slab_epoch). Accept promote only if watermark_ts < now - safe_delay. safe_delay tuned per-cluster.

susan: edge-case: what if watermark stale due to clock skew? insist on max-clock-drift and prefer reading a small ground-truth key when in doubt. also emit "probe_uncertain" metric and treat as probe_fail to be conservative.

omar: one more tradeoff — sample probes might miss rare writes; we need to accept small probability of false-negative. capture that in SLO: allow no more than X RAWR regressions per million promotions. product/SRE ok with that?

susan: we should also add a limited backoff circuit for prefixes that repeatedly fail probe (hot flip-flop): penalties escalate (lease denial window grows) and we emit "prefix_promo_banned" for a short TTL.

nina: final note on debugging: expose debug endpoint /_debug/promotes?tenant=... that shows WAL moves, probe snapshots, and recent probe results. make entries compact so ops can triage quickly.

ops-bot: alert candidate created: "promotion_fence_probe_latency_p95" (severity: medium) and "promotion_stuck_entries" (severity: high).

felix: ok, can someone own the RFC? include: watermark definition, probe implementation details, WAL state transitions, invariants, metrics, rollout and kill-switch playbook, and audit checksum design.

nina: I'll author RFC and add a small sim harness to model probe false-negative rates. cc @susan for ops runbook and @omar for WAL idempotency design. thanks everyone. :rocket:
